title: Large payees registered at a home or on an empty lot
question: Which firms paid $1 million or more by the City have no registered premises other than a home or an empty lot?
finding: Of 1,015 payees paid $1 million or more since fiscal 2019 that could be placed at one registered San Francisco address, 34 are registered only on parcels the assessor classes as a house, condominium, small flats or an empty lot; for 10 a contract notice or directory entry gives the same address. The largest confirmed: Treeline Security Inc. ($22.8 million, mostly GSA - City Administrator, house, condominium or small flats). Most are consultants and small builders whose office is the owner's home; nothing here shows work billed from a place that does not exist.
how: A payee is placed by its business registration when exactly one registry account carries its name. Each open location is looked up in the City's address system to get its parcel, and the parcel's use on the 2025 assessor roll is read. A payee is listed when every location is a single-family dwelling, condominium or small flats (live/work classes left out) on which Planning's land-use file (DataSF c5ge-t6pj) records no commercial space, or every location is classed as vacant land on which Planning records no homes or commercial space. The match is treated as confirmed only when a City contract notice or a certified-firm directory gives the same street address for the same name.
limits: Running a firm from home is ordinary for consultants, interpreters and small contractors, and a registration address is where the tax bill goes, not where the work is done. The roll's "vacant" class also covers sites under construction and City-owned land (several rows are housing partnerships building on such sites, or a City vendor housed in a public building). Homes are never listed: the table gives the kind of parcel and the neighborhood only. The payee-to-registry join is by name unless the last column says otherwise.

columns.t: How the payee and the registration were joined
